items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the personal property law, in relation to holders in due course and loan assignees; and to amend the financial services law, in relation to authorizing the superintendent of financial services to promulgate regulations governing motor vehicle retail installment contracts
items.lawCode: Amd §302, Pers Prop L; amd §302, Fin Serv L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5506

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the personal property law, in relation to holders in due
course and loan assignees; and to amend the financial services law, in
relation to authorizing the superintendent of financial services to
promulgate regulations governing motor vehicle retail installment
contracts

PURPOSE:

This bill slightly increases liability on loan assignees in automobile
financing transactions and holders in due course in automobile financing
transactions by providing that plaintiffs who prevail in cases against
assignees in automobile transactions and holders in due course in auto-
mobile transactions may be entitled to attorney's fees exclusive of caps
on assignee and holder in due course liability.  This bill also holds
assignees in automobile financing transactions and holders in due course
in automobile financing transactions jointly and severally liable with
dealerships in instances where these parties have knowledge of fraud in
motor vehicle transactions and do not attempt to mitigate the
plaintiff's damages in such cases.  This bill also empowers the super-
intendent of the Department of Financial Services to regulate retail
installment contracts.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends Subdivision 9 of section 302 of the personal property
law to specify that (1) attorney's fees are exclusive of any cap on
suits against loan assignees and holders in due course, and authorizes
courts to award attorney's fees in these cases to prevailing plaintiffs,
and (2) in cases where loan assignees and holders in due course are
aware of fraud in motor vehicle financing transactions, and do not take
action to mitigate the plaintiff's damages resulting from fraud, these
lenders will be jointly and severally liable for fraud stemming from
these transactions.

Section 2: Amends Section 302 of the financial services law to authorize
the superintendent of the Department of Financial Services to promulgate
regulations which direct persons offering and servicing retail install-
ment contracts, to establish certain guidelines for the review and
acceptance of such contracts, including the submission of suspicious or
fraudulent applications, the verification of retail buyer income and
liabilities, direct contact with the retail buyer prior to acceptance,
and meaningful response to consumer complaints.

Section 3: This act shall take effect on the first of January next
succeeding the date on which it shall have become a law.

EXISTING LAW:

Under current law, assignees and holders in due course generally have
their liability capped to the amount of the loan purchased. Under
current law, the Department of Financial Services currently does not
have general jurisdiction over retail installment contracts.

JUSTIFICATION:

In many cases, consumers are defrauded by auto dealerships who create
fraudulent loan applications stating false income levels or employment
histories. Consumers are then stuck with auto loans they could have
never been expected to afford and must then sue auto dealerships to
become financially whole. In some cases, dealerships close their doors
and default on these obligations, and lenders associated with the deal-
erships turn a blind eye to this fraud and consumer abuse.

Lender liability is usually limited under the holder in due course rule
and rules concerning loan assignees. Thus, consumers are left to recover
from dealerships (who often shut their doors or default), even when, in
some cases, lenders are complicit with fraud. In order to deter fraud
and inaccurate applications, lender liability must be increased. By
making attorney's fees exclusive of the normal cap on assignee liability
and holder in due course liability, consumers will be able to access
legal counsel in more cases where auto dealers have engaged in fraud,
and banks that purchase auto loans will be more careful about monitoring
lending practices and the legitimacy of loan applications. Due to
increased liability, lenders who are aware of and complicit with auto
loan fraud will now have a strong disincentive to continue working with
abusive and predatory dealerships.

Additionally, there are no universal standards designed to combat
consumer abuse in retail installment contracts. This legislation allows
the superintendent of the Department of Financial Services to promulgate
such standards, requiring lenders to establish procedures for flagging
suspicious or potentially fraudulent applications, verify retail buyer
income and liabilities, etc.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the personal property law, in relation to loan assignees
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5506A

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the personal property law, in
relation to loan assignees

 PURPOSE :

This bill slightly increases liability on loan assignees in automobile
financing transactions by providing that plaintiffs who prevail in
cases against assignees in automobile transactions may be entitled to
attorney's fees exclusive of caps on assignee liability, at the
court's discretion.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Amends Subdivision 9 of section 302 of the personal
property law to specify that attorney's fees are exclusive of any cap
on suits against loan assignees, and authorizes courts to award
attorney's fees in these cases to prevailing plaintiffs.

Section 2: This act shall take effect on the first of January next
succeeding the date on which it shall have become a law.

 EXISTING LAW :

Under current law, assignees generally have their liability capped to
the buyer's amount owing to the assignee.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In many cases, consumers are defrauded by auto dealerships who create
fraudulent loan applications stating false income levels or employment
histories. Consumers are then stuck with auto loans they could have
never been expected to afford and must then sue auto dealerships to
become financially whole. In some cases, dealerships close their doors
and default on these obligations, and lenders associated with the
dealerships turn a blind eye to this fraud and consumer abuse.

Banks and lenders in automobile transactions have heavy involvement in
creating the terms under which these contracts are executed, and
enable dealers to transact business by providing routes of financing.
Even though they are technically assignees because the dealer executes
the financing contract, the dealer very quickly sells the note to the
assignee, and the banks and financing companies are de facto lenders
in these transactions. Lender liability is limited under the assignee
rule in the Motor Vehicle Retail Instalment Sales Act. Thus, consumers
are left to recover from dealerships (who sometimes shut their doors
or default), even when, in some cases, lenders are complicit with
fraud. By making attorney's fees exclusive of the normal cap on
assignee liability, consumers will be able to access legal counsel in
more cases where auto dealers have engaged in fraud, and banks that
purchase auto loans will be more careful about monitoring lending
practices and the legitimacy of loan applications. Due to increased
liability, lenders who are aware of and complicit with auto loan fraud
will now have a strong disincentive to continue working with abusive
and predatory dealerships.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.

summary: Limits loan assignee liability with regard to motor vehicle retail installment contracts.
